original.target_description: Experiment 2: explicit paper-and-pencil evaluations of CS+ versus CS− among undergraduate women retained after contingency-awareness exclusions; subsequent t test of the explicit measure.

n.sample_role: Participants (undergraduate women); exact analytic n for explicit t test cannot be established consistently.
n.exclusions: 56 recruited; authors report excluding 6 aware participants from all analyses (implying 50 retained), but explicit t test is printed with 48 degrees of freedom. No further missing-data exclusion is documented here.
n.quote: Fifty-six undergraduate women participated in the experiment. / we excluded the data from these 6 participants from all analyses / t(48)

es.location: p. 416 (PDF p. 4), Results, subsequent t tests

p.location: p. 416 (PDF p. 4), Results, subsequent t tests

replication.target_description: Single multilaboratory replication: primary random-effects meta-analysis of self-reported evaluative preference for CSpos over CSneg, after original Olson and Fazio awareness exclusion criterion. The replication changes the explicit measurement task and is described by authors as a close conceptual replication.

n.sample_role: Participants included across twelve laboratories in the primary meta-analysis.
n.exclusions: 9.2% excluded overall as printed; surveillance-error exclusions and original Olson and Fazio awareness criterion applied.
n.location: p. 7, Primary analyses (continued from p. 6); Fig. 2a p. 6

reported_success.location: p. 7, Primary analyses, conclusion for original awareness criterion
reported_success.quote:

authors’  awareness  exclusion  criterion  was  employed,

notes: Original title and authors verified in retrieved primary paper; replication title and authors verified in supplied cache. Original PDF text has corrupted mathematical glyphs; equals signs normalized in statistic quotes. Exact original analytic n is left null because recruitment/exclusion accounting implies 50 whereas reported t(48) implies 49 for a one-sample test. No n is calculated or substituted. Replication success verdict refers specifically to primary original-criterion analysis; secondary criteria did not yield significant EC effects and authors qualify the broader unaware-EC interpretation. Replication uses self-reported preference rather than the original rating scale; this design difference is explicitly acknowledged. Original n quotation uses slash-separated excerpts from the same page.
